title: Garment workers can now buy OMS rice at Tk 30 a kilo
excerpt: The Food Ministry's special sale runs from 66 trucks in six industrial areas, with a 10 kg monthly limit for each worker.

image.alt: File photo: rice sacks from the Ministry of Food at an OMS subsidised sale in Dhanmondi, Dhaka (2021)
image.credit: File photo: Press Information Department, Government of Bangladesh, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain)

content:
Garment workers can buy rice at Tk 30 a kilogram under a special Open Market Sale (OMS) programme that started on Friday, 13 November, the Ministry of Food said in a press release reported by The Daily Star. Each worker can buy up to 10 kg a month.

How it works

  • Where: 66 trucks in Dhaka, Savar, Dhamrai, Gazipur, Narayanganj and parts of Chattogram district.
  • Trucks by area: Gazipur 30, Narayanganj 10, Chattogram 10, Savar eight, Dhaka six, Dhamrai two.
  • Quantity: five tonnes a truck, 330 tonnes in all, according to the release as reported.
  • Hours: 10am to 12:30pm and 2:30pm to 5pm, until further notice and while stocks last.
  • Who can buy: workers must show a factory identity card and sign a register.

The sale comes amid weeks of unrest over pay. The minimum wage board, formed this month, has met twice, and the workers' representative has proposed a minimum wage of Tk 32,000 a month. Owners have threatened to close factories if the unrest continues.

Why it matters

Subsidised rice eases food costs for some of the lowest-paid urban workers while the new wage is negotiated. NGOs working with garment workers on nutrition, childcare and rights can help workers, especially women, learn where and when the trucks sell. The 10 kg monthly limit covers only part of a family's rice needs.

What to watch

Whether the programme expands to more areas or larger amounts, and the wage board's next meeting.
